wages.text: He said the federal minimum wage should rise so full-time workers can afford a decent life.
wages.quote: “It’s time to raise the minimum wage so everyone who works hard can afford a decent life.”

housing.text: His campaign says Congress should make it easier to build homes and increase the housing supply.
housing.quote: Congress should make it easier to buy a home and easier to build one.

health.text: His campaign supports expanding Medicare coverage to include vision and dental care.
health.quote: Expand Medicare to cover vision and dental so seniors are no longer forced to dig into their savings or skip care entirely because of holes in their coverage.

energy.text: He supports an all-of-the-above energy strategy focused on lower consumer costs and domestic production.
energy.quote: We need a comprehensive, all of the above strategy that creates jobs and increases energy independence while bringing down costs for consumers today.

tax.text: Marshall praised tax cuts in the 2025 reconciliation bill and said he believes cutting taxes helps the economy grow.
tax.quote: They don’t realize that when you cut taxes, the economy grows.

wages.text: He voted against a motion to increase the federal minimum wage and introduced legislation he said would protect workers from union bosses.
wages.quote: protects workers from overbearing and unaccountable union bosses and small business owners from unelected bureaucrats in Washington.

housing.text: Marshall supported a Senate bill that encourages zoning and permitting changes to expand housing supply.
housing.quote: Encouraging state and local governments to streamline permitting and zoning processes that limit housing development.

schools.text: He supported school-choice scholarships and expanded education-savings flexibility.
schools.quote: I think the Republican Party has shown our support for this school choice in the Working Family Tax Cuts Bill.

safety.text: He introduced a bill allowing school-relief funds to pay for security measures and armed school resource officers.
safety.quote: such as locks, panic buttons, individual room security systems, video surveillance, and hiring and paying the salaries of armed school resource officers.

sentencing.text: He joined legislation creating sentencing enhancements and an additional prison term for specified federal offenses involving flag burning.
sentencing.quote: which would enact sentencing enhancements for individuals who burn the American flag in the course of committing a federal offense.

immigration.text: He has supported border security measures including a border wall and stricter enforcement of immigration laws.
immigration.quote: We must secure our southern border and stop drugs and violent crime from coming into our nation. I support President Trump’s efforts to build the wall, and secure our communities.

guns.text: He voted against a federal gun-reform bill and criticized its red-flag-law provisions.
guns.quote: Kansans expect me to protect their Constitutional freedoms in the U.S. Senate, and I will not sacrifice those freedoms for this gun grabbing scheme.

abortion.text: Marshall said he believes life begins at conception and welcomed the end of Roe v. Wade as a new beginning for unborn children.
abortion.quote: Because of these wonderful moments and experiences, I believe life begins at conception. In fact, this is why today’s historic decision signals a new beginning for millions of unborn American children.

gender.toward: rules based on sex at birth
gender.text: He introduced legislation to restrict participation in girls’ and women’s sports based on biological sex.
gender.quote: I find it un-American to allow biological boys to compete against biological girls when it comes to athletics.

cannabis.text: In a candidate questionnaire, Marshall strongly disagreed with legalizing recreational marijuana.
cannabis.quote: I support the legalization of recreational marijuana. Strongly Disagree

health.text: He opposed eliminating private health insurance and described his health care approach as increasing consumer choice and innovation.
health.quote: I support the elimination of private healthcare insurance. Strongly Disagree

energy.text: He introduced a bill to block regulations that he said would slow oil and gas production and raise gasoline prices.
energy.quote: that’s what my legislation does is to have a regulatory pause on anything that would slow down our oil and gas energy.

voting.text: He backed legislation requiring proof of citizenship to register for federal elections and voter ID.
voting.quote: It’s a straightforward bill that requires proof of citizenship to register to vote in our federal elections, along with voter ID and validating mail-in ballots.

tax.text: He said taxes, especially the sales tax, should be greatly reduced.
tax.quote: All taxes, especially the sales tax, should be greatly reduced.

safety.text: He opposed redirecting police funds to mental-health and community programs, while also saying more police funding does not necessarily increase safety.
safety.quote: I do not support de-funding the police. However, i do not believe that giving the police more money necessarily increases public safety.

immigration.text: He described immigration as needing to be measured and orderly and said illegal immigration must not be tolerated.
immigration.quote: Immigration should be measured and orderly. Illegal immigration must not be tolerated. Open borders are a national security risk.

guns.text: He said he would not vote for more national gun laws and opposed limits on lawful gun owners.
guns.quote: I pledge that as a United States Senator, I shall never vote for more national gun laws.

abortion.text: He said abortion should be allowed only when necessary to save the mother's physical life or after the preborn child has died.
abortion.quote: Abortion should be allowed if imminently necessary to save the physical life of the mother. It also should be allowed if the preborn child has died.

health.text: He opposes government involvement in health care and says free enterprise should operate in the sector.
health.quote: The government should get out of the healthcare business. Free enterprise should be allowed to operate in the healthcare sector.

energy.text: He agreed that stricter environmental rules can cost jobs and hurt the economy, and supports fracking.
energy.quote: A) Stricter environmental laws and regulations cost too many jobs and hurt the economy.

voting.text: He supports paper ballots and absentee voting for people who need it, but wants to eliminate early voting.
voting.quote: I would continue to allow absentee ballots for those who need them, but would eliminate early voting.

sources: christianpost.com · hamiltonforkansas.com · marshall.senate.gov · ivoterguide.com · kclyradio.com · onyourballot.vote411.org
